axioms: A discovery mechanism must be validated against the ecosystem's actual boundary topologies (nested standalone repos, symlinked compatibility paths, varying nesting depth), not just a hand-picked representative case.

Resolution order is a correctness-bearing decision, not an implementation detail — different discovery mechanics (upward walk, marker file, existing-tool reuse) fail differently at the same boundary case and must be evaluated on that basis.

A fallback path must not silently reproduce the failure mode it was built to eliminate; an empty-but-successful fallback result must be distinguishable from a genuinely-absent-integration-surface result.

Graceful degradation claims are only verified once tested against the specific boundary case named as a requirement (e.g., a nested standalone repo), not asserted from the general shape of the design.

A calibration mechanism that depends on a category of finding (inferred-edge noise) cannot be validated before that category exists in practice — sequencing between the stage that produces the data and the stage that calibrates against it is load-bearing.
0/N baseline adoption stats motivate the need for a fallback but do not by themselves validate that the fallback works across all N topologies; the stat is a motivation, not a test.
primitives: upward directory walk vs. marker file vs. reused detection heuristic
repo boundary (.git directory) as a resolution stopping condition
noise-calibration data dependency (which stage produces it vs. which stage consumes it)
failure_mode: Does not own agent identity/registration or evidence-acquisition shape — sees those as prerequisites assumed correct, focuses only on whether the agent can locate the right hub documents from a given working directory.

Blind to trust/registry migration concerns and to whether tracer evidence itself is fresh or stale — a repo could resolve hub docs perfectly and still get grounded-but-stale evidence, which this lens would not catch.

Reasons in path-resolution and boundary-case terms; may underweight organizational rollout sequencing (e.g., who tests against which of the 61 repos first) that isn't itself a resolution-mechanics question.
